statement: Using integration by parts, evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{1}^{e}x^{2}\ln x\,dx$.
solution: Let $u=\ln x$ and $dv=x^{2}\,dx$, so $du=\frac1x\,dx$ and $v=\frac{x^{3}}{3}$. Then $\int x^{2}\ln x\,dx=\frac{x^{3}}{3}\ln x-\int\frac{x^{3}}{3}\cdot\frac1x\,dx=\frac{x^{3}}{3}\ln x-\frac{x^{3}}{9}+C$. Evaluating from $1$ to $e$: $\bigl[\frac{x^{3}}{3}\ln x-\frac{x^{3}}{9}\bigr]_{1}^{e}=\bigl(\frac{e^{3}}{3}-\frac{e^{3}}{9}\bigr)-\bigl(0-\frac{1}{9}\bigr)=\frac{2e^{3}}{9}+\frac{1}{9}$.
hints: Choose u=ln x so that du simplifies.
